method: Headlines from the source feed, read by Claude: summary and four beats in Blue Street's own words from each article's headline and public text; impact = which way the headline pushes each market (dir bullish/bearish/mixed, strength 1 mild, 2 clear, 3 strong). Evidence, not a call.

USD.text: The dollar ended the week slightly higher, near its strongest since March 2025, because markets see a Federal Reserve rate rise on December 9 as all but certain after hot inflation and strong growth figures. Odds of a second rise in January, now about 64%, are what could push it further.

EUR.text: The euro sits near $1.095, close to its lowest since April 2025, because the Federal Reserve looks set to raise rates before the European Central Bank. Inflation slowed far more than expected in France and Spain on Friday, November 27, but households now expect prices to rise 3.5% over the next year and Bundesbank head Joachim Nagel said rates may still need to rise in December.

GBP.text: The pound is heading for its best week against the euro in almost a month, near 83.5 pence per euro, as markets still expect a Bank of England rate rise in mid-December and euro area inflation cools. Against the dollar it stays near $1.31, close to its lowest in a year, because a Federal Reserve rise on December 9 looks all but certain.

JPY.text: The yen slipped to about 159.6 per dollar on Friday, November 27, near its weakest of the week, after Tokyo inflation came in a little under forecast and was driven mostly by fuel. Talk of a Bank of Japan rate rise on December 18 and Japan's warnings that it may step in near 160 are slowing the fall, while dearer oil remains a cost.

CHF.text: The Swiss franc rose to its strongest against the euro this month as falling AI shares and the Iran war sent money to safe places. Iran called the drone deaths in Kuwait a set-up on Friday, November 27, as President Trump said Iran still has a chance to talk, while bets on more Federal Reserve rate rises keep the franc softer against the dollar.

CAD.text: The Canadian dollar has bounced from a 19-month low as all six of Canada's biggest banks expect a Bank of Canada rate rise on December 9 and Brent oil holds in the mid-$90s. Growth figures on Monday, November 30 are expected to show the economy slowed sharply in July to September, which could test those rate bets.

AUD.text: The Australian dollar is near 66.4 US cents after its lowest in a year, helped by the biggest jump in business investment since 2011, inflation of 4.9% that keeps rates high, and Chinese factory profits up 20.1% in October. Falls in AI shares and proposed US tariffs on China and others still weigh.

NZD.text: The New Zealand dollar sits near 55 US cents, just above its lowest since 2009, after a 10-day slide stopped on Thursday, November 26. Markets price a likely Reserve Bank of New Zealand rate rise to 3% and Chinese demand looks firmer, but US rates rising faster still pull money away.

XAU.text: Gold closed Friday, November 27 up about 2.4% near $3,654 an ounce and 3.3% higher on the week, bouncing hard from a 15-month low on Wednesday, November 25 as the Gulf war and falling AI shares brought buyers back. Holiday trading was thin, and a near-certain Federal Reserve rate rise on December 9 still weighs on a metal that pays no interest.

OIL.text: Brent crude settled at $95.44 on Friday, November 27, down 1.2% on the day but up about 3% on the week, its first weekly rise in November, after Houthi attacks on Saudi refineries and a US blockade of Iran that keeps Gulf shipping disrupted. OPEC+ meets on Sunday, November 29 and is expected to leave output unchanged, while forecasts of a surplus still act as a brake.

items.headline: Gold ends Friday up 2.4% near $3,654, its first weekly gain in a while, with silver up 5%
items.story_title: Gold and Federal Reserve rate rises
items.summary: Spot gold closed in New York on Friday, November 27 up about 2.4% at roughly $3,654 an ounce, finishing the week 3.3% higher after hitting a 15-month low two days earlier. Silver jumped more than 5%.

beats.was: Gold fell to about $3,427 on Wednesday, November 25, its lowest in 15 months, as markets bet the Federal Reserve will raise US rates on December 9, which hurts a metal that pays no interest.
beats.happened: In thin trading after the US Thanksgiving holiday, spot gold rose 2.43% to about $3,654 by the New York close on Friday, November 27, up 3.25% on the week. Silver rose 5.3% to about $43.75, and shares of gold miners jumped.
beats.means: Buyers came back quickly once gold looked cheap, helped by the war around Iran and falls in AI shares. Light holiday trading can exaggerate moves, so the bounce is less solid than it looks.
beats.fx: A firmer gold price tends to lift the Australian dollar, since Australia is a big gold producer, and shows some demand for safe places to park money.

impact.why: Gold rebounded sharply from a 15-month low and ended the week higher.
Higher gold prices help Australia's export earnings.

items.watch: The US jobs report for November on Friday, December 4, and the Federal Reserve decision on December 9.

items.headline: Brent settles 1.2% lower at $95.44 on Friday but keeps a weekly gain before Sunday's OPEC+ meeting
items.story_title: Oil supply: surplus vs Gulf attacks
items.summary: Brent crude ended Friday, November 27 down 1.2% at $95.44 a barrel and US crude fell to $83.08, yet Brent still rose about 3% on the week after attacks on Saudi refineries and tankers in the Gulf.

beats.was: Oil had fallen for most of November on forecasts of more supply than demand, then climbed from Wednesday, November 25 as Yemen's Houthi rebels hit Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura and Jazan refineries and ships were damaged near the Strait of Hormuz during the Iran war.
beats.happened: January Brent settled at $95.44 on Friday, November 27, down 1.2%, and US crude settled at $83.08, down 0.7%. Brent gained about 3% for the week, its first weekly rise in November. OPEC+, the producer group led by Saudi Arabia and Russia, meets on Sunday, November 29 and is expected to keep output targets unchanged into early 2027.
beats.means: Traders took some money off the table before the weekend, but the Gulf attacks have stopped oil's slide. The International Energy Agency still expects a surplus this quarter, which caps how far prices can climb.
beats.fx: Oil in the mid-$90s supports the Canadian dollar and keeps fuel costs high for importers like Japan and the euro area.

impact.why: Prices dipped on Friday but held a weekly gain on Gulf supply worries.
Oil near $95 supports Canada's export income.

items.watch: The OPEC+ meeting on Sunday, November 29, and any new attacks on Gulf refineries or shipping.

items.headline: Dollar ends the week a little higher as markets see a Fed rate rise on December 9 as near-certain
items.story_title: The Fed's rate rises and the strong dollar
items.summary: The dollar index rose 0.25% to about 104.0 on Friday, November 27, for a small weekly gain, with markets pricing a 99% chance that the Federal Reserve raises rates on December 9 and about 64% for another rise in January.

beats.was: The Federal Reserve, the US central bank, has its main rate at 3.75%–4.00% and markets expect it to raise rates again because US inflation is running hot.
beats.happened: In thin post-holiday trading on Friday, November 27, the dollar index, which tracks the dollar against six major currencies, rose 0.25% to about 104.04. The euro slipped to about $1.093 and the dollar rose to about 159.5 yen. Futures prices put the odds of a December 9 Fed rate rise at 99% and of a second rise in January at about 64%.
beats.means: The dollar's strength rests on the US raising rates faster than most other countries. With a December rise fully expected, the next push would have to come from the January odds.
beats.fx: A firm dollar keeps the euro near its lowest since April 2025 and the yen close to 160, the level where Japan has warned it may step in.

impact.why: Near-certain Fed rate rise keeps the dollar firm, though it is already expected.
The dollar sits near 160 yen as the gap in rates stays wide.
The euro slipped toward $1.093 as US rates look set to rise first.

items.watch: US November jobs figures on Friday, December 4, and the Fed decision on Wednesday, December 9.

items.headline: Economists expect Canada's growth to have slowed by more than half in July to September, with figures due Monday, November 30
items.story_title: Bank of Canada: inflation and the rate path
items.summary: Economists expect Statistics Canada to report on Monday, November 30 that the economy grew at about a 1.3%–1.5% yearly pace in July to September, down from 3.3% in April to June.

beats.was: Markets and all six of Canada's biggest banks expect the Bank of Canada to raise rates on December 9 to fight inflation, even as the job market has softened and trade talks with the US are unsettled.
beats.happened: Ahead of Statistics Canada's growth figures on Monday, November 30, forecasters, including economists at BMO and Desjardins, expect growth of about 1.3% to 1.5% at a yearly pace for the third quarter, down from 3.3%. Canada lost a net 34,900 jobs over the period. Trade Minister Dominic LeBlanc said talks with the US have restarted, with a December 31 deadline.
beats.means: A slower economy is already expected, so only a much weaker or stronger number would shift bets on the December rate rise. This is a preview, not the result.
beats.fx: A weak growth figure could trim bets on a Bank of Canada rate rise and soften the Canadian dollar, while a solid one would back the case for a December 9 rise.

impact.why: A preview: slower growth is expected, and the actual figure on Monday, November 30 decides the push.

items.watch: Canada's third-quarter growth figures on Monday, November 30, and the Bank of Canada decision on December 9.

items.headline: US goods trade gap widens to $149.5 billion in October as imports jump
items.story_title: America's widening trade gap
items.summary: The US bought far more goods from abroad than it sold in October, leaving a gap of $149.5 billion, up 10.7% from September and well above forecasts, as imports of machines and computers for AI kept surging.

beats.was: US imports have climbed through 2026 as companies buy chips, servers and equipment to build AI data centres, while the US has proposed new tariffs on several trading partners.
beats.happened: Early figures from the US Census Bureau, released on Friday, November 27, showed the goods trade gap widened to $149.5 billion in October from $135.1 billion in September, against forecasts near $133 billion. Imports rose 6.1% and exports 3.2%, and imports of capital goods were 80% higher than a year earlier.
beats.means: A much bigger trade gap takes a little off US growth in October to December, because money spent on imports does not count as US output. It also shows how much the AI buildout relies on foreign-made equipment.
beats.fx: A wider gap means more dollars flowing abroad, a mild weight on the dollar, but it barely dents the view that the Federal Reserve raises rates on December 9.

impact.why: A far wider goods trade gap than forecast slightly trims the US growth picture.

items.watch: The full US trade report, including services, and US jobs data for November on Friday, December 4.

items.headline: Two ECB rate-setters say rates may need to rise again as soon as December
items.story_title: Will the ECB raise rates one last time in December?
items.summary: Joachim Nagel, head of Germany's Bundesbank, said euro area inflation could stay above 3% into 2027 and rates may need to rise again in December, and Slovenia's central bank governor said two rises so far may not be enough.

beats.was: The European Central Bank has raised its deposit rate twice this year, to 2.5%, as the Iran war pushed energy costs up, then held in October. Its next decision is on December 17.
beats.happened: On Friday, November 27, Bundesbank President Joachim Nagel said the ECB may have to do more and could raise rates as soon as December, since he expects inflation to stay above 3% in 2027. Primoz Dolenc, Slovenia's central bank governor and also an ECB rate-setter, said the two rises so far are not enough and that dearer energy is spreading into service prices.
beats.means: These comments came hours after inflation in France and Spain slowed far more than forecast. They tell markets that some ECB members still see inflation lasting well above the 2% goal and are not ready to stop raising rates.
beats.fx: Firm talk of another ECB rise supports the euro and softens the blow from the weaker inflation figures, though the Federal Reserve still looks set to move first on December 9.

impact.why: Two ECB rate-setters, including Germany's central bank head, pointed to another rate rise as soon as December.

items.watch: Germany's November inflation on Monday, November 30, the euro area figure on Tuesday, December 1, and the ECB decision on December 17.

items.headline: Yen slips near its weakest of the week after Tokyo inflation comes in a little soft
items.story_title: The yen, the Bank of Japan and intervention risk
items.summary: The yen weakened to about 159.6 per dollar on Friday, November 27, close to its weakest of the week, after Tokyo's main inflation measure rose less than expected.

beats.was: The Bank of Japan's rate is 1.25%, and markets expect a rise at its December 17-18 meeting. Japan stepped into the currency market to buy yen in late July and early August, and traders see 160 per dollar as the level where it may do so again.
beats.happened: Tokyo prices excluding fresh food rose 2.9% from a year earlier in November, the most in 16 months but just short of the 3.0% forecast. Leaving out energy as well, the rate eased to 2.5% from 2.6%, so much of the rise came from dearer fuel.
beats.means: Inflation driven mainly by energy gives the Bank of Japan a weaker case for raising rates quickly. Meanwhile the US Federal Reserve is expected to raise rates on December 9, keeping the gap in interest rates wide in the dollar's favour.
beats.fx: The yen drifts back towards 160 per dollar, the area where Japan's warnings of action carry most weight, so further falls may be slower.

impact.why: Tokyo's core inflation came in just under forecast and was driven mostly by energy.
An expected Fed rate rise keeps US rates far above Japan's.

items.watch: Whether the yen reaches 160 per dollar, and the Bank of Japan meeting on December 17-18.

items.headline: Pound heads for its best week against the euro in almost a month
items.story_title: Bank of England: how far do rates rise?
items.summary: The pound rose to about $1.312 and to its firmest against the euro in weeks on Friday, November 27, helped by a rebound in world shares and softer inflation in France and Spain.

beats.was: The pound had dropped to near its lowest in a year against the dollar because the US Federal Reserve looks set to raise rates on December 9, while Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey said on Wednesday, November 25 that inflation may not climb as high if energy prices settle.
beats.happened: The euro slipped about 0.25% to 83.48 pence, set for a weekly fall, and the pound edged up to about $1.312. Two other Bank of England rate-setters, Catherine Mann and Clare Lombardelli, sounded firmer on inflation than Bailey, and US tech shares were set for a weekly gain of about 4% after falling 10% the week before.
beats.means: Markets still expect the Bank of England to raise rates at its meeting in mid-December, while slower inflation in France and Spain makes a European Central Bank rise look less pressing. Calmer share markets also help the pound, which tends to suffer when investors get nervous.
beats.fx: The pound gains most against the euro, where the gap between the two central banks' plans is widening. Against the dollar it is only a small lift.

impact.why: Firm talk from Bank of England rate-setters and calmer markets lifted the pound against the euro.
The euro fell against the pound after inflation slowed in France and Spain.

items.watch: The Bank of England's December meeting, and UK inflation figures before it.

items.headline: Inflation slows far more than expected in France and Spain as fuel gets cheaper
items.story_title: Will the ECB raise rates one last time in December?
items.summary: Prices in France rose 2.9% from a year earlier in November, down from 3.4%, and in Spain 4.1%, down from 4.9%, both well below forecasts, as fuel costs fell.

beats.was: Euro area inflation had climbed to about 4% because the Iran war pushed up energy prices, and notes from the European Central Bank's October meeting leaned towards a rate rise on December 17.
beats.happened: Early November figures on Friday, November 27 showed French inflation at 2.9% against about 3.2% expected, and Spain's at 4.1% against about 4.7% expected. Spain's core rate, which leaves out food and energy, fell to 2.6% from 3.1%, and French prices fell 0.7% in the month.
beats.means: Cheaper fuel is pulling inflation down quickly in two of the euro area's biggest economies, and Spain's core figure shows the slowdown is not only about energy. That gives the European Central Bank less reason to raise rates again in December.
beats.fx: Lower inflation weakens the case for a December rise, which weighs on the euro, especially against the pound and the dollar, where rate rises still look likely.

impact.why: Inflation fell well below forecasts in France and Spain, making an ECB rate rise in December less certain.
The euro fell against the pound on the softer figures.

items.watch: Germany's and Italy's November inflation, then the full euro area figure on Tuesday, December 1, and the ECB decision on December 17.

items.headline: Dollar holds below Monday's 20-month high as investors take some money off the table
items.story_title: The Fed's rate rises and the strong dollar
items.summary: The dollar index, which tracks the dollar against six major currencies, held near 103.7 on Friday, November 27, about flat for the week and below the 20-month high it hit on Monday, November 23.

beats.was: The dollar climbed about 1.7% in November as hot inflation and growth revised up to 4.3% made a US Federal Reserve rate rise on December 9 look all but certain.
beats.happened: Investors cut back on bets that the dollar will keep rising, even after the strong figures. Some think the Fed will raise rates once in December but be careful about going much further, with US tech shares still nearly 20% below their October highs.
beats.means: Much of the good news for the dollar is already in its price, so the rally has paused. A single, careful rate rise would support the dollar without pushing it much higher.
beats.fx: A pause in the dollar gives the euro, pound and other majors some room to steady after their November falls.

impact.why: The dollar is still high on Fed rate rise bets, but investors are trimming bets on further gains.

items.watch: US jobs figures for November on Friday, December 4, and the Fed decision on December 9.

items.headline: Euro area shoppers expect faster inflation over the next year, ECB survey finds
items.story_title: Will the ECB raise rates one last time in December?
items.summary: A European Central Bank survey published on Friday, November 27 found households expect prices to rise 3.5% over the next year, up from 3.1%, while they expect their pay to grow only 0.6%.

beats.was: The European Central Bank has raised its deposit rate twice this year, to 2.5%, as the Iran war pushed energy costs up. It watches what households expect, because those hopes can feed into wage demands and prices.
beats.happened: The ECB's monthly survey of about 19,000 adults, covering October and published on Friday, November 27, showed expected inflation for the next 12 months rising to 3.5% from 3.1%. Expectations three years out edged up to 3.0%, five years out stayed at 2.5%, and expected income growth fell to 0.6% from 1.1%.
beats.means: People expect prices to keep rising well above the ECB's 2% goal while their own incomes lag. That is the kind of result that pushes the ECB toward one more rate rise on December 17, even after softer inflation in France and Spain the same day.
beats.fx: Rising price expectations back the case for another ECB rise, which supports the euro a little.

impact.why: Households expect faster inflation, which supports another ECB rate rise on December 17.

items.watch: Germany's November inflation on Monday, November 30, the euro area figure on Tuesday, December 1, and the ECB decision on December 17.

items.headline: Trump calls the upgraded US growth figure fake and asks for an investigation
items.story_title: The Fed's rate rises and the strong dollar
items.summary: President Donald Trump said on Thursday, November 26 that the upward revision to US economic growth was a deliberate error and called for a probe, without giving evidence.

beats.was: The Bureau of Economic Analysis, the government office that measures US output, raised its estimate of growth in July to September to a 4.3% yearly pace from 3.4% on Wednesday, November 25, a bigger change than usual.
beats.happened: In a Thanksgiving post on social media, Trump said the earlier, lower figure from before the election was wrong on purpose and wanted it investigated. The office published both numbers on its normal schedule, and its staff has shrunk by about a fifth since 2024.
beats.means: The higher figure itself backs a Federal Reserve rate rise on December 9. The attack on the statistics office adds a worry about how far investors can trust official US data, though no inquiry has been announced.
beats.fx: Doubts about US data are a small mark against the dollar, but the strong growth number behind the row still supports it.

impact.why: Strong growth backs a Fed rate rise, while a political attack on the data office adds a small trust worry.

items.watch: The third growth estimate on December 23, and the Fed's decision on December 9.

items.headline: Gold jumps 2.7% to about $3,632 and silver leaps 8% in thin holiday trading
items.story_title: Gold and Federal Reserve rate rises
items.summary: US gold futures rose 2.7% to about $3,632 an ounce early on Friday, November 27, and silver jumped more than 8%, as both metals bounced hard from 14-month lows.

beats.was: Gold had slid to its lowest in about 14 months earlier in the week because markets expect the Federal Reserve to raise US interest rates on December 9, which makes a metal that pays no interest less appealing.
beats.happened: Gold futures in New York climbed to about $3,632 an ounce from $3,535, and silver rose from about $40 to $43.42. Trading was thin because many US traders were away for the Thanksgiving holiday.
beats.means: Buyers came back after the steep drop, helped by the war around the Gulf and the slide in AI shares. Moves in thin holiday markets can be large and may not last once full trading returns.
beats.fx: A sharp rebound in gold points to fresh demand for safety, which tends to help the Swiss franc and the yen, while firmer metal prices give a small lift to the Australian dollar.

impact.why: Gold rose about 2.7% in a single session, its biggest bounce in weeks.
Renewed buying of gold hints at more demand for safe places to hold money.
Australia mines a lot of gold, so higher prices help its export earnings a little.

items.watch: Whether the bounce holds when US markets fully reopen on Monday, November 30, and the Fed's decision on December 9.

items.headline: China's factory profits grow 20.1% in October, the fastest in five months
items.story_title: China's economy and the commodity currencies
items.summary: Profits at Chinese industrial firms rose 20.1% from a year earlier in October, up from 14.4% in September, in figures out on Friday, November 27, Beijing time.

beats.was: China is the biggest buyer of Australian iron ore and a major market for New Zealand's farm goods, so signs of strength or weakness there move both currencies. Profits had already been growing through 2026, by 15.5% in the first nine months.
beats.happened: China's statistics office said industrial profits grew 20.1% in October alone, a sharp pickup from 14.4% in September. For January to October together, growth rose to 16.0%.
beats.means: Chinese factories are earning more, which suggests steady demand for raw materials. It comes as the US plans new tariffs on China and other partners, which could cut into that strength next year.
beats.fx: Firmer Chinese industry gives mild support to the Australian and New Zealand dollars, though both are still pulled lower by rising US rates.

impact.why: Stronger profits at Chinese factories point to steady demand for Australian iron ore.
Better business in China, a big buyer of New Zealand goods, helps a little.

items.watch: China's official factory survey for November at the end of the month, and how far the planned US tariffs on China go.

items.headline: Iran calls the deadly Kuwait drone attack a set-up as Trump says Iran still has a chance to talk
items.story_title: The Iran war and the Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Iran's foreign minister Abbas Araghchi called the drone incident that killed two Italian workers in Kuwait suspicious and a pretext for wider war, while President Trump said the US is close to winning and is giving Iran a chance to negotiate.

beats.was: The war between Iran and the US and Israel began with US-Israeli strikes in late February. On Thursday, November 26, Kuwait said debris from Iranian drones it shot down killed two Italian technicians, and the European Union called for more pressure on Iran.
beats.happened: In reports published on Friday, November 27, Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi called the Kuwait incident suspicious and said it looked like a plan prepared in advance to widen the war. US President Donald Trump said the US has victory in hand and is giving Iran a chance to come to the table.
beats.means: Iran is denying blame while the US mixes threats with an open door to talks. Neither side is backing down, but the talk of a deal keeps alive the hope that fighting near the Strait of Hormuz could ease.
beats.fx: Hints of talks soften the war premium in oil a little, while the sharp words from both sides keep some demand for safe places such as the Swiss franc.

impact.why: Trump's offer of talks could calm supply fears, but Iran's denial and the trading of blame keep the risk alive.
Sharp words over a deadly attack keep some money in safe places.

items.watch: Whether Iran takes up talks, whether Kuwait responds to the attack, and the OPEC+ meeting on Sunday, November 29.

items.headline: Iran says a tanker blew up on a mine in the Strait of Hormuz and another turned back
items.story_title: The Iran war and the Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Iran's Revolutionary Guards navy said on Friday, November 27 that an oil tanker exploded after hitting a mine in the Strait of Hormuz and a second tanker was forced to turn back.

beats.was: The US and Israel went to war with Iran on February 28. A deal signed in June stalled over shipping through the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow route for about a fifth of the world's oil, and Iran says it will only fully reopen it if attacks stop and US sanctions are lifted.
beats.happened: Iran said the two tankers tried to slip through an unapproved route north of Ghavam Island on the morning of Friday, November 27. It did not name the ships or give any details on damage or crews, and the claim has not been confirmed by others. It follows a similar Iranian claim on Thursday, November 26.
beats.means: Iran is signalling that ships which avoid its approved routes will be hit, which keeps the strait risky and slows any recovery in Gulf oil flows. Without confirmation, the market treats it as added risk rather than a proven loss of supply.
beats.fx: Each new threat to Gulf oil helps lift crude, which supports oil exporters like Canada and is a cost for big importers like Japan and the euro area.

impact.why: An unconfirmed Iranian claim of a second tanker hit by a mine in two days.
Higher oil prices help Canada's export earnings.
Japan buys almost all its oil abroad, so dearer crude is a cost.

items.watch: Whether shipping firms or other governments confirm the explosion, and the OPEC+ meeting on Sunday, November 29.

items.headline: US military says it fired on and disabled a cargo ship leaving Iran in breach of its blockade
items.story_title: The Iran war and the Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: US Central Command said it disabled the engines of the Palau-flagged cargo ship Pacific Archer in the Gulf of Oman on Thursday, November 26, after it left Iran's port of Bandar Abbas. It is at least the 15th ship stopped this way since the US blockade began in April.

beats.was: The United States has blockaded Iran's ports since April during the Iran war, turning back ships and sometimes firing on those that try to get through. Shipping through the nearby Strait of Hormuz, a key route for Gulf oil, is well below normal.
beats.happened: US Central Command, which runs American forces in the Middle East, said on Friday, November 27 that it fired on the Pacific Archer on Thursday, November 26, stopping its engines. The crew was not hurt. The US says it has now redirected 158 merchant ships. Iran's Revolutionary Guards separately claimed, without proof, that a tanker hit a mine in the strait.
beats.means: The blockade is being enforced as hard as ever, so there is no sign yet of the Gulf shipping lanes getting back to normal. A single disabled cargo ship, though, is part of a known pattern rather than a new escalation.
beats.fx: Ongoing trouble in Gulf shipping keeps a floor under oil, which helps the Canadian dollar and weighs on oil importers like Japan.

impact.why: Firm enforcement of the blockade keeps Gulf supply risks alive.
Japan imports almost all its oil, so lasting Gulf trouble raises its costs.

items.watch: Whether attacks on ships near the Strait of Hormuz pick up, and any sign of US–Iran talks.

items.headline: Canadian dollar holds steady as oil and rate rise bets offset a smaller current account surplus
items.story_title: Bank of Canada: inflation and the rate path
items.summary: The Canadian dollar held near C$1.4245 per US dollar on Friday, November 27, as dearer oil and bets on a Bank of Canada rate rise offset news that Canada's surplus with the rest of the world nearly halved in July to September.

beats.was: The Bank of Canada raised its rate to 2.5% in October, its first rise in three years, and Governor Tiff Macklem has warned that high oil prices could keep inflation lasting. Its next decision is on December 9.
beats.happened: On Friday, November 27, the Canadian dollar traded in a narrow range around 70.2 US cents, with swaps pricing about an 80% chance of a December rate rise. Statistics Canada said the same day that the current account surplus, which sums trade, income and transfers with other countries, fell to C$4.5 billion in July to September from C$8.8 billion, well short of forecasts near C$9.9 billion.
beats.means: A smaller surplus means less money flowing into Canada from abroad, a small negative. But the bigger forces for the currency, oil near $96 and a likely rate rise, still point the other way.
beats.fx: Rate rise bets and oil keep the Canadian dollar steady near the top of its recent range, with the weaker surplus only a minor drag.

impact.why: Rate rise bets and dearer oil support it, while a much smaller current account surplus weighs a little.

items.watch: Canada's July to September growth figures on Monday, November 30, and the Bank of Canada decision on December 9.

items.headline: Tokyo inflation comes in at 2.8% in November, below the 3% expected
items.story_title: The yen, the Bank of Japan and intervention risk
items.summary: Prices in Tokyo rose 2.8% from a year earlier in November, a little under the roughly 3% economists expected, in figures out on Friday, November 27, Tokyo time.

beats.was: Tokyo's consumer prices come out about three weeks before the national figures and are watched as an early read on Japan's inflation. The Bank of Japan, with its rate at 1.25%, is widely expected to raise it at the meeting ending December 18.
beats.happened: Overall prices in Japan's capital rose 2.8% in the year to November, against forecasts near 3%. Prices leaving out fresh food, the measure the Bank of Japan watches most, rose 2.9%, up from 2.6% in October.
beats.means: Inflation stays well above the Bank of Japan's 2% goal and is still rising on the measure it cares about most, so the case for a December rate rise holds. The small miss on the overall figure gives no extra push.
beats.fx: The figures change little for the yen, which stays near 159 per dollar and close to the 160 level where Japan has warned it may step in.

impact.why: Overall prices came in a bit soft, but the main measure rose and still backs a December rate rise.

items.watch: The Bank of Japan's decision on December 18, and any warnings from Japan's finance ministry if the dollar nears 160 yen.

items.headline: Two Italian workers killed as Kuwait shoots down Iranian drones
items.story_title: The Iran war and the Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Kuwait said on Thursday, November 26 that two Italian technicians died when debris from Iranian drones it shot down fell on a key site. Iran denied attacking.

beats.was: The war between Iran and the US and Israel began with US-Israeli strikes in late February. Kuwait hosts US forces and was last targeted by drones on November 18.
beats.happened: Kuwait's Defence Ministry said falling debris from intercepted drones killed two Italian workers for the defence firm Rheinmetall and hurt a Kuwaiti and a Pakistani worker on Thursday, November 26. Kuwait called it a breach of its sovereignty and kept the right to respond. Iran's military denied any attack.
beats.means: Deaths of Western civilians in a Gulf state widen the war beyond shipping and Saudi oil sites. No damage to Kuwaiti oil output or exports was reported.
beats.fx: More fighting in the Gulf keeps a risk premium in oil and supports safe places such as the Swiss franc.

impact.why: Another Gulf oil producer is drawn in, though no supply loss was reported.
A wider war adds to demand for safe places.

items.watch: Whether Kuwait answers the attack, and talks led by Qatar and Pakistan to calm the fighting.

items.headline: Saudi-led coalition says Houthis attacked Jazan refinery, hits back in Yemen
items.story_title: Oil supply: surplus vs Gulf attacks
items.summary: The Saudi-led coalition said Yemen's Houthi rebels attacked Saudi Arabia's Jazan refinery on Thursday, November 26, and that it destroyed the missile launcher used.

beats.was: Yemen's Houthi rebels, who back Iran, have stepped up attacks on Saudi Arabia since Tuesday, November 24. On Wednesday, November 25 they claimed a drone strike on Ras Tanura, the kingdom's biggest refinery, and Saudi forces said they downed four drones there.
beats.happened: The coalition said the Houthis struck the Jazan refinery on the Red Sea coast on Thursday, November 26, and that it then destroyed a ballistic missile launch site at Yemen's Hodeidah port. No damage to the refinery or to Saudi output was given.
beats.means: A second Saudi refinery targeted in two days keeps the fear of lost Gulf supply alive, even while big stock builds point to a surplus next year.
beats.fx: A supply scare lifts oil, which helps the Canadian dollar and Norway's krone and is a cost for Japan and the euro area.

impact.why: A second Saudi refinery targeted in two days, with no output loss confirmed.
Higher oil prices lift income for Canada, a big oil exporter.
Japan imports nearly all its oil, so supply scares raise its costs.

items.watch: Any word from Saudi Aramco on damage at Jazan, and the OPEC+ ministers' meeting on Sunday, November 29.

items.headline: Eurozone leaders back Hernández de Cos to succeed Lagarde at ECB
items.story_title: Will the ECB raise rates one last time in December?
items.summary: Euro area leaders chose Pablo Hernández de Cos, a former governor of Spain's central bank, on Thursday, November 26 to follow Christine Lagarde as European Central Bank president from February 2027.

beats.was: Christine Lagarde said on October 29 she will step down as European Central Bank president on February 7, 2027, before her term ends. The bank has raised rates twice this year, with euro area inflation at 4% in October, twice its 2% goal.
beats.happened: At a summit in Brussels, leaders backed Hernández de Cos, 55, who now runs the Bank for International Settlements and led the Bank of Spain from 2018 to 2024. He beat Klaas Knot, former head of the Dutch central bank, after the Netherlands dropped its objection. The same package names Laurence Boone and Markus Brunnermeier to the bank's board. The choice still needs formal sign-off.
beats.means: The question of who leads the bank next year is settled without a fight. Some analysts see him as a little softer on inflation than Knot, but mainly as a pragmatic centrist, so no big shift in rate policy is expected.
beats.fx: A smooth handover removes a source of doubt for the euro. A slightly softer leader at the margin could trim rate-rise bets for 2027, but the December 17 decision is still the main driver.

impact.why: A calm, expected choice for the next ECB president, seen as a centrist, so little change to the rate path.

items.watch: Formal approval of the new ECB board, and the ECB rate decision on Thursday, December 17.

items.headline: All six of Canada's biggest banks now expect a Bank of Canada rate rise in December
items.story_title: Bank of Canada: inflation and the rate path
items.summary: TD became the last of Canada's six biggest banks to forecast a Bank of Canada rate rise on December 9, after Governor Tiff Macklem warned about inflation.

beats.was: The Bank of Canada raised its rate to 2.5% in October, its first rise in three years, as energy costs from the Middle East war pushed up prices. On Tuesday, November 24 Governor Tiff Macklem stressed that inflation is lasting and firms may pass on higher energy costs.
beats.happened: By Thursday, November 26 all six big banks (RBC, TD, Scotiabank, BMO, CIBC and National Bank) expected another rise on December 9. CIBC and BMO moved their call up from January earlier in the week of November 23, and TD followed. Markets put the odds near 80%.
beats.means: A December rise is now the near-unanimous view, so much of it is already in prices. Canada's July-September growth figures and November jobs report, both due next week, could still change the call.
beats.fx: Higher Canadian rates make the Canadian dollar more rewarding to hold, though the US Federal Reserve is also expected to raise rates on December 9.

impact.why: Bank forecasts catch up with a December rate rise markets mostly expect already.

items.watch: Canada's July-September GDP and November jobs report next week, then the Bank of Canada decision on Wednesday, December 9.

items.headline: Sterling steady as dollar takes a breather
items.story_title: Bank of England: how far do rates rise?
items.summary: The pound held near $1.31 on Thursday, November 26 after falling in 13 of the past 16 sessions, while traders added to bets on Bank of England rate rises in December and February.

beats.was: The pound has lost more than 2% against the dollar in November, back to levels last seen a year ago, as markets price a Federal Reserve rate rise on December 9. The Bank of England raised its rate to 4% earlier in November.
beats.happened: Sterling was little changed at about $1.31 and near 83.8 pence per euro in quiet holiday trading. Money markets now lean toward back-to-back Bank of England rises in December and February, and price three more rises by September 2027. A Santander Asset Management strategist said part of the pound's drop came from the fall in share prices, and that its longer-run value now looks better.
beats.means: UK rate bets are rising, which gives the pound a floor, but the dollar's own rate story has been stronger. The slide has paused rather than turned.
beats.fx: Firmer Bank of England bets are a mild support for the pound. The direction against the dollar still hangs on the Fed decision on December 9.

impact.why: Traders now lean toward two more Bank of England rate rises, in December and February.

items.watch: The Bank of England decision on Thursday, December 17, and the Fed decision on Wednesday, December 9.

items.headline: EUR/CHF breakdown as safe-haven demand outweighs ECB–SNB rate repricing
items.story_title: AI stocks and the mood in markets
items.summary: The Swiss franc rose sharply against the euro in the week to Thursday, November 26, with the euro falling to about 0.907 francs before bouncing to near 0.915, as nervous investors sought a safe place for money.

beats.was: On Monday, November 23, a euro bought about 0.9485 Swiss francs. Since then the Nasdaq has fallen about 3.7% over a week on worries about AI stocks, South Korea's main share index has lost 7.4%, and Iran has tightened its grip on the Strait of Hormuz.
beats.happened: The euro broke below its November low of 0.9122 francs and touched 0.9070 before recovering to about 0.9153 by Thursday, November 26. The move came mostly from franc buying, since the euro was flat against the dollar. At the same time, the gap between expected European Central Bank and Swiss National Bank rate rises has narrowed, after Swiss inflation rose to 1.5% in October.
beats.means: Fear in markets is doing more for the franc than rate differences are. Both central banks are expected to raise rates in December, so the safe-place demand is the bigger driver for now.
beats.fx: The franc firms against the euro when shares fall and war worries grow, and softens again when calm returns. The Swiss National Bank decides on Thursday, December 10.

impact.why: Safe-place buying pushed the franc to its strongest against the euro this month.
Lost ground to the franc as stock markets fell, though steady against the dollar.

items.watch: The Swiss National Bank decision on Thursday, December 10, and the ECB decision on Thursday, December 17.

items.headline: Bank of England warns AI financing threatens financial stability, puts hyperscalers' exposure at over $4T
items.story_title: AI stocks and the mood in markets
items.summary: The Bank of England warned on Thursday, November 26 that borrowing to build AI is growing complex and hard to see into, putting the big tech firms' total exposure at just over $4 trillion.

beats.was: AI-linked shares make up just over half the value of the S&P 500, and they have fallen sharply since Monday, November 23 on worries about how the AI build-out is paid for. The Bank of England publishes a Financial Stability Report twice a year on risks to the financial system.
beats.happened: In its November report, the bank's Financial Policy Committee said AI funding is becoming circular and opaque, and that with higher interest rates several weak spots could give way at once. Bank staff put the potential exposure of firms such as Alphabet, Amazon, Microsoft, Meta and Oracle, including leases and guarantees, at just over $4 trillion. Borrowing by AI builders is almost double its 2025 level, and the cost of insuring some AI firms' debt against default hit records in the days before.
beats.means: A major central bank is now openly flagging AI debt as a risk to the wider system, which adds weight to the worries already hitting tech shares. It is a warning, not a policy change, so it does not alter UK rate plans.
beats.fx: Worries about AI debt tend to hurt currencies tied to global growth, like the Australian and New Zealand dollars, and help safe places like the yen and Swiss franc. Sterling itself barely reacts to the report.

impact.why: A central-bank warning on AI debt adds to the risk-off mood that weighs on growth-linked currencies.
More worry about markets tends to draw money to the franc.
A stability warning, not a rate signal, so little direct effect on the pound.

items.watch: How AI shares trade when US markets reopen on Friday, November 27, and the Bank of England rate decision on Thursday, December 17.

items.headline: (ECB) Monetary policy accounts
items.story_title: Will the ECB raise rates one last time in December?
items.summary: Notes from the European Central Bank's October 28-29 meeting, published on Thursday, November 26, show many rate-setters could have backed a rate rise then, which supports the case for one on December 17.

beats.was: The European Central Bank raised rates in June and September, then held in October. Euro area inflation jumped to 3.8% in September, pushed up by dearer energy, while growth was slowing.
beats.happened: The written record of the October meeting showed many members said they could have supported a rise already. They worried that energy costs would spread into other prices, and noted the euro's slide against the dollar adds to import costs. They also saw growing risks to growth.
beats.means: The notes point to a rise at the December 17 meeting, which markets already expect. They add little new, but they show the bank's leaning has not softened.
beats.fx: Confirms a December rise that is mostly priced, a mild support for the euro. The bigger driver of the euro is still the gap with faster US rate rises.

impact.why: Many rate-setters were ready to raise rates in October, backing a December rise that is mostly priced.

items.watch: The ECB's decision and new forecasts on Thursday, December 17.

items.headline: Oil Slides Despite Shipping Mine Claims and Supply Risks
items.story_title: Oil supply: surplus vs Gulf attacks
items.summary: Brent crude slipped below $94 a barrel by mid-morning in Europe on Thursday, November 26, giving back part of Wednesday's 3.5% jump even as Yemen's Houthi rebels claimed an attack on Saudi Arabia's biggest refinery.

beats.was: Brent rose 3.5% to $94.61 on Wednesday, November 25 after tankers hit mines in the Strait of Hormuz and Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia spread. Oil is still about 13% lower than a month ago on worries about too much supply next year.
beats.happened: Brent fell about 0.9% to $93.79 by 0939 GMT on Thursday, November 26 and US crude dipped to about $83.33. The Houthis said they struck the Ras Tanura refinery, though Saudi Arabia and its state oil firm Aramco did not confirm it. Iran's army said a tanker hit a mine and caught fire in a closed-off area of the Strait. US crude stocks rose 1.1 million barrels last week.
beats.means: Attacks keep adding risk, but buyers took profits after a big jump, and plenty of supply caps prices. Analysts see Brent moving roughly between $88 and $97 for now.
beats.fx: A small dip after a big rise leaves oil-linked currencies like the Canadian dollar with most of their support. US markets are closed for Thanksgiving, so trading is light.

impact.why: Profit-taking after a 3.5% jump, while an unconfirmed Houthi refinery attack keeps supply risk alive.
Oil eased a little but held most of Wednesday's gains.

items.watch: The OPEC+ meeting on Sunday, November 29 on output for 2027.

items.headline: OPEC+ may roll over current oil output targets at its Sunday meeting
items.story_title: Oil supply: surplus vs Gulf attacks
items.summary: OPEC+, the group of big oil producers led by Saudi Arabia and Russia, may keep its output targets unchanged when ministers meet on Sunday, November 29, two people close to the talks said on Thursday, November 26.

beats.was: OPEC+ sets how much oil its members aim to pump. The Iran war has damaged Gulf oil sites and disrupted exports from its Middle East members, while many forecasters still expect too much oil worldwide in 2027.
beats.happened: Two sources told Reuters on Thursday, November 26 that the group may simply roll over its current targets, though no decision has been made. The research firm Rapidan also expects no change, with big quota choices pushed into 2027 because of war damage and uncertainty over how long the fighting lasts.
beats.means: A hold would mean no extra oil from the group soon, leaving prices driven mainly by attacks in the Gulf. It would also put off the question of a supply glut next year.
beats.fx: Steady output keeps oil supported for now, a small help for oil-exporting currencies such as the Canadian dollar and a small cost for oil buyers such as Japan.

impact.why: No extra supply is planned while the war limits Gulf exports.
Firm oil prices help Canada's export income.
Japan imports nearly all its oil, so dearer crude is a cost.

items.watch: The OPEC+ ministers' meeting on Sunday, November 29, and whether it says anything about output for 2027.

items.headline: Tanker struck by projectile while transiting Strait of Hormuz, UKMTO says
items.story_title: The Iran war and the Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: The UK Navy's shipping safety office (UKMTO) said on Thursday, November 26 that a tanker leaving the Gulf was hit by an unidentified projectile in the Strait of Hormuz on Wednesday, November 25. The crew were safe and no spill was reported.

beats.was: Since the US-Israeli strikes on Iran in February 2026, ships in the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow route for about a fifth of the world's oil, have come under repeated attack. Iran's Revolutionary Guards have claimed several tankers hit mines since Tuesday, November 24, but outside agencies have confirmed fewer incidents than Iran claims.
beats.happened: UKMTO, which collects reports from ships in the region, said local authorities told it an outbound tanker was struck about 18 nautical miles east of Khasab, a port on Oman's tip of the strait. All crew were accounted for and no damage to the sea was reported. The ship was not named and no one was blamed.
beats.means: This is an attack confirmed by an outside agency, not only an Iranian claim, so the risk to ships in the strait is real. It was a projectile, not a mine, so it does not prove Iran's mine claims. One more attack keeps ship insurance costs high and gives oil buyers a reason to pay up for supply.
beats.fx: More risk to Gulf oil flows tends to lift crude, which helps oil exporters like Canada and is a cost for big importers like Japan and the euro area.

impact.why: A confirmed attack on a tanker in Hormuz adds to supply risk, though no oil was lost.
Higher oil prices help Canada's export earnings.
Japan buys almost all its oil abroad, so dearer crude is a cost.

items.watch: Whether UKMTO names the ship or says who fired, and the OPEC+ meeting on Sunday, November 29, where ministers set 2027 output.

items.headline: European stocks rally as tech and banks rebound, tariff fears ease
items.story_title: New US tariffs
items.summary: European shares rose about 1.4% on Thursday, November 26, as tech and bank stocks bounced and proposed US tariffs on the EU looked likely to stay at the 15% rate agreed last year.

beats.was: On Wednesday, November 25 European shares fell more than 1% as US inflation came in hot, AI shares slid and the US proposed new import taxes on 14 trading partners, including the EU.
beats.happened: The STOXX 600 index of big European companies rose 1.4% early on Thursday, November 26. Chip and tech firms gained nearly 2%, and banks such as Deutsche Bank rose about 3%. Reports suggested US duties on EU goods will likely be capped at the 15% the two sides agreed last year.
beats.means: If the EU is spared a fresh jump in US import taxes, one risk to Europe's growth fades. Shares also followed Wall Street's late recovery from its AI sell-off.
beats.fx: Calmer trade news and firmer shares are a mild support for the euro and for currencies that track risk appetite, like the Australian dollar. US markets are shut for Thanksgiving, so moves are thin.

impact.why: US tariffs on the EU look likely to stay at the agreed 15%, easing a growth worry.
Stocks bounced after the AI sell-off, a better mood for risk-sensitive currencies.

items.watch: The final US tariff list, with written comments due by January 5, 2027.

items.headline: Australian dollar finds support in data centre boom, kiwi edges away from 17-year low
items.story_title: Australian inflation and the Reserve Bank of Australia
items.summary: Business investment in Australia jumped by the most since 2011 in July to September, driven by data centres, and the Australian dollar edged up to about 66.4 US cents on Thursday, November 26.

beats.was: The Australian dollar fell to its lowest in a year on Wednesday, November 25, near 65.6 US cents, and is down about 5.6% in November as AI shares slid and US rates looked set to rise. Inflation of 4.9% in October had already ruled out early rate cuts by the Reserve Bank of Australia.
beats.happened: Company spending on buildings and equipment rose far more than expected in the third quarter, led by data centres, though much of the money went on imported equipment. The Australian dollar rose 0.2%. The New Zealand dollar was flat near 54.9 US cents, ending a 10-day losing run just above its lowest since 2009.
beats.means: Strong investment points to an economy with more pace than feared, which backs the case that Australian rates stay high for longer. Markets do not expect a rate cut for many months. In New Zealand, swaps price about an 80% chance of a quarter-point rate rise to 3% at the next decision.
beats.fx: Better local news gives the Australian dollar some footing after a heavy month, though swings in AI shares still drive it day to day. The kiwi has stopped falling but has not turned.

impact.why: The biggest jump in business investment since 2011 supports keeping rates high.
A 10-day slide paused near a 17-year low, with a rate rise priced but not yet delivered.

items.watch: The Reserve Bank of Australia's last rate decision of the year in December.

items.headline: Saudis down missiles targeting capital after Yemen port strikes
items.story_title: The Iran war and the Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Saudi Arabia said its air defences shot down two ballistic missiles aimed at Riyadh around midnight going into Thursday, November 26, after Saudi-led strikes on Yemen's Hodeidah port and Houthi attacks on the Red Sea ports of Jeddah and Jazan.

beats.was: Yemen's Houthi rebels, allied with Iran, have stepped up attacks on Saudi Arabia during the Iran war. They claimed a strike on Saudi Arabia's Ras Tanura refinery on Wednesday, November 25, which Saudi officials have not confirmed, and a drone hit a Riyadh office tower on Tuesday, November 24, injuring 11.
beats.happened: An explosion was heard in Riyadh after an air-raid alert. The Saudi-led coalition said it also downed a cruise missile in the west and a drone near Jeddah port, with no civilian injuries. The Houthis said they hit Jeddah and Jazan in reply to coalition strikes on Hodeidah, Yemen's main port.
beats.means: The fighting between Saudi Arabia and the Houthis is widening, with the Saudi capital and Red Sea ports now targets. That adds a second risk to Gulf oil supply on top of tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz.
beats.fx: More risk to Saudi supply keeps a floor under oil, which helps oil-exporting currencies like the Canadian dollar and supports safe places like the Swiss franc.

impact.why: Attacks reaching Saudi Arabia's capital and Red Sea ports raise the risk to Gulf supply.
Firmer oil supports the currency of a big oil exporter.
A wider Gulf conflict adds demand for safe places.

items.watch: The OPEC+ ministers' meeting on Sunday, November 29, which sets oil output for 2027.

items.headline: Dollar steady as sliding yields temper safe-haven bid
items.story_title: The Fed's rate rises and the strong dollar
items.summary: The dollar held steady in Asian trading on Thursday, November 26, a little above a one-week low, as a drop in US bond yields took the edge off its pull as a safe place.

beats.was: The dollar index hit a 19-month high on Monday, November 23, after Nvidia's board put co-founder Jensen Huang back in charge and AI shares rallied. Hot US inflation figures on Wednesday, November 25 left markets almost sure the Federal Reserve will raise rates on December 9.
beats.happened: The dollar index sat flat near 103.7. The US 10-year bond yield fell as much as 0.1 point to about 4.8%, its lowest in two and a half months. The Australian dollar climbed back above 66 US cents after nearly a one-year low, and the euro held near $1.097.
beats.means: Lower US yields shrink the dollar's interest-rate edge, but markets still expect a Fed rate rise in December and another early in 2027. With US markets shut for Thanksgiving, trading is thin and moves can be jumpy.
beats.fx: The dollar is resting rather than turning. The yen, Swiss franc and Canadian dollar kept their gains from Wednesday, November 25.

impact.why: Falling bond yields offset firm bets on a Fed rate rise in December.
Back above 66 US cents after its weakest level in almost a year.
Held a 0.5% safe-place gain from Wednesday, November 25.

items.watch: The Federal Reserve's rate decision on December 9, which markets expect to be a quarter-point rise.

items.headline: Houthi strike on Saudi Jazan refinery kills a worker and forces a partial shutdown
items.story_title: Oil supply: surplus vs Gulf attacks
items.summary: Saudi Arabia's energy ministry said on Thursday, November 26 that a strike on its Jazan refinery killed one worker, injured others and forced part of the plant to shut.

beats.was: Yemen's Houthi rebels, who are backed by Iran, have been firing missiles and drones at Saudi oil sites during the wider war with Iran, adding to fears about Gulf oil supply.
beats.happened: Saudi state news said one worker from Nepal died and several were hurt at the Jazan refinery in the south of the country, and some of its units were halted. The Saudi-led coalition blamed the Houthis, promised a firm military answer and said it destroyed a Houthi missile launcher in Yemen. Iran denied any role in a separate deadly drone attack in Kuwait.
beats.means: Saudi fuel output has now been hit directly, not just threatened. Brent crude barely moved on the news early on Friday, November 27, because some of the damage was already in the price after a 3.5% jump on Wednesday, November 25.
beats.fx: Lost Saudi refining keeps oil supported, which helps the Canadian dollar and weighs on big energy buyers such as Japan and the euro area.

impact.why: Part of a Saudi refinery is shut after a deadly strike.
Firmer oil helps Canada, a big oil exporter.
Japan buys almost all its oil abroad, so dearer energy is a cost.

items.watch: How fast the Jazan refinery restarts, and what OPEC+ producers decide at their meeting on Sunday, November 29.

items.headline: Dollar rally pauses for Thanksgiving
items.story_title: The Fed's rate rises and the strong dollar
items.summary: The dollar held just below its highest since March 2025 on Thursday, November 26, as US markets shut for Thanksgiving, while the Swiss franc slipped 0.4% against it.

beats.was: The dollar has climbed for weeks as markets bet the Federal Reserve will raise rates by a quarter point on December 9 and again early in 2027. Hot core PCE inflation for October and a big upward revision to US growth in the third quarter, both out on Wednesday, November 25, added to those bets.
beats.happened: With US markets closed, the dollar index sat near 103.7. The euro was steady near $1.098 after its lowest since April 2025 earlier in the week, sterling was about $1.31 and the dollar near 159.25 yen. The franc weakened 0.4% to about 0.834 per dollar. One Mizuho strategist described the dollar's strength as defensive, after the US proposed new tariffs on 14 trading partners on Wednesday, November 25.
beats.means: The holiday pause does not change the story: US rates look set to rise faster than elsewhere, which keeps money flowing to the dollar. Thin trading can make moves look bigger than they are until US markets reopen on Friday, November 27.
beats.fx: The dollar stays firm against most major currencies. The franc lost ground to the dollar on the day, even as it gained against the euro.

impact.why: Holds near its highest since March 2025 on bets of more Fed rate rises.
Slipped 0.4% against the dollar in quiet holiday trading.
Steady near $1.098, close to its lowest since April 2025.

items.watch: The return of US trading on Friday, November 27, and the Fed rate decision on Wednesday, December 9.

items.headline: Oil rises on supply concerns as Iran claims mine strikes on ships
items.story_title: The Iran war and the Strait of Hormuz
items.summary: Brent crude edged up to about $94.70 a barrel early on Thursday, November 26, after Iranian state media said another oil tanker hit a sea mine and caught fire in the Strait of Hormuz.

beats.was: Iran has tightened its control of the Strait of Hormuz, the narrow sea route for about a fifth of the world's oil. Brent rose 3.5% on Wednesday, November 25 after Yemen's Houthi rebels said they attacked Saudi Arabia's biggest refinery, Ras Tanura.
beats.happened: Iran's Fars news agency, citing the Iranian army, said a tanker struck a mine and caught fire inside a zone Iran calls restricted. The claim was not confirmed by others. Brent rose 0.1% and US crude 0.4% to about $84 a barrel in quiet Asian trade.
beats.means: Each new attack claim adds to the risk that Gulf oil flows, which had begun to recover, get cut again. Against that, oil is still down nearly 20% in November on worries about too much supply next year.
beats.fx: Dearer oil helps oil exporters like Canada and is a cost for big importers like Japan and the euro area.

impact.why: An unconfirmed claim of another tanker hit by a mine in Hormuz.
Higher oil prices help Canada's export earnings.
Japan buys almost all its oil abroad, so dearer crude is a cost.

items.watch: The OPEC+ meeting on Sunday, November 29, where ministers set 2027 output, and whether other sources confirm the mine strike.

items.headline: BOJ's Tamura signals chance of faster-pace interest rate hikes
items.story_title: The yen, the Bank of Japan and intervention risk
items.summary: Naoki Tamura, one of the Bank of Japan's nine rate-setters, said on Thursday, November 26 the bank may need to raise rates faster if inflation runs too hot, and that a rise could come in December.

beats.was: The Bank of Japan raised its rate in June and September to 1.25%, then held in October. Markets widely expect a rise to 1.5% at the meeting ending December 18. Tamura is one of the two members most keen on higher rates.
beats.happened: Tamura said costlier raw materials from the Middle East conflict, a weak yen and strong demand linked to artificial intelligence are pushing prices up. He said the bank's rate is still some way below a level that neither helps nor holds back the economy.
beats.means: His words back a December rate rise and hint at more after it, but he is known for wanting higher rates, and he mostly confirmed what markets already expect. The dollar stayed near 159 yen.
beats.fx: Talk of faster Japanese rate rises gives the yen some support, though the gap with much higher US rates still holds it near its weakest levels.

impact.why: A rate-setter backs a December rise and hints at a faster pace after it.
Narrower rate gap with Japan over time, but the Fed is still raising too.

items.watch: Tokyo consumer prices on Friday, November 27, an early read on Japan's inflation before the December 18 decision.

items.headline: Stock market today: Dow, S&P 500, Nasdaq sink on hot inflation, new Trump tariffs as chip rout continues
items.story_title: AI stocks and the mood in markets
items.summary: US shares fell hard on Wednesday, November 25, with the Nasdaq down about 4% and the S&P 500 down nearly 3% by late morning in New York, as chip stocks kept sliding and fresh inflation and tariff news hit.

beats.was: US tech shares had already dropped sharply on Tuesday, November 24, with Nvidia down 9%, ending a long rally built on artificial intelligence. Bringing back Jensen Huang as Nvidia's chief executive on Monday, November 23 had briefly lifted shares.
beats.happened: Nvidia fell almost 9% more and an index of chipmakers lost over 6%. The Nasdaq-100 neared a fall of 20% from its peak, the usual line for a bear market. A gauge of expected share swings, the VIX, jumped about 28% to near 34. Core PCE inflation came in at 3.3% against 3.2% expected, and the US proposed new tariffs of up to 20% on 14 trading partners. Investors moved into US government bonds, pulling the 10-year yield down about 0.07 points to 4.82%.
beats.means: Markets are now dealing with two pressures at once: a sharp fall in the shares that drove the past rally, and a Federal Reserve still set to raise rates on December 9. Lower bond yields show some money already looking for safety.
beats.fx: A deep share sell-off tends to hurt risk-linked currencies like the Australian and New Zealand dollars and help the yen. Falling US yields take a little shine off the dollar's rate support.

impact.why: A deep fall in US shares drives money out of risk-linked currencies.
The kiwi tends to fall when share markets sell off hard.
Share market stress brings some money back to the yen.
Rate-rise bets hold, but US bond yields fell as investors sought safety.

items.watch: Whether the chip sell-off spreads further, and thin trading around the US Thanksgiving holiday on Thursday, November 26, with a half-day on Friday, November 27.

items.headline: New Zealand Dollar rebounds from 2009 low ahead of confidence data
items.story_title: The kiwi and the RBNZ
items.summary: The New Zealand dollar bounced to just under 55 US cents by Wednesday, November 25, after ten straight daily falls took it to its lowest since March 2009 on Monday, November 23.

beats.was: The Reserve Bank of New Zealand surprised markets on October 28 by holding its rate at 2.75% in a 4-3 vote, when a rise had been almost fully expected. US rates are higher and the Federal Reserve looks set to raise them again on December 9.
beats.happened: The kiwi won back about a quarter of its slide over two days, though it dipped near 54.5 cents on Wednesday, November 25 as tech shares fell across Asia, with South Korea's main index down over 6%. A New Zealand consumer confidence survey from ANZ and Roy Morgan comes on Thursday, November 26.
beats.means: The bounce is small next to the slide. The gap between New Zealand and US rates still pulls money away from the kiwi.
beats.fx: The kiwi stays weighed down by low local rates and by any fall in share markets, with short bounces when selling runs out.

impact.why: A small bounce from a 17-year low, but the rate gap with the US still weighs.

items.watch: The ANZ-Roy Morgan consumer confidence survey for November on Thursday, November 26.
